Lines are '<code>|<text>' as in Story.cs: W Wallit, S Slice, Y Yo Bot, M Mega Yo Bot, K Courier, P Plated Alpha, F Foreman, H Half-Built, V Server, R Registrar, O Order-Bearer, N narration; codes come from Resources/Cast/cast.json. tagline: Where things that should not exist are given an address.

department.arc: A process with no face. Ch1 it only stamps. Ch2 it answers from behind a wall. Ch3 it is a floor that makes crews. Ch4 it is politeness: it serves, it waits. Ch5 it is a form nobody signed. Ch6 it is denied. Ending: a thing it cannot strike is given a door. It never hates anyone; it only clears.
department.unseen: The creature behind the order is never seen, named or quoted.

arcs.start: Wants a refund and a sender to bill.
turns: Ch1: takes the stamp on himself for Slice
Ch2: finds the postmark that is half his
Ch3: sees he could be one of the cleared things
Ch4: has no joke when Slice says before you
Ch5: uses the Department's stamp against it
Ch6: reads the order and says DENIED
arcs.end: Chooses an address for others, not for himself: he gives the stamp away.

arcs.start: Stay in the circle. Explains nothing.
turns: Ch1: names what pays him
Ch2: leaves the ring to follow him, staked
Ch3: her longest beat is It isn't
Ch4: says the order was aimed at her before him
Ch5: lets him use the stamp, asks only whether he has the nerve
Ch6: files the circle herself
arcs.end: Admits she needs him, in one word, and writes the door number.

turns: Ch1: reads the notice, lands it, is broken
Ch5 (flag notice_kept): its notice is the page Wallit stamps first

arcs.end: Its last line is a question it cannot answer: defeat?

scenes.name: The Stamp
scenes.beat: The stamp falls on leather; a wallet rolls into the ring.
lines: N|Out of the dark comes a stamp: RETURN TO SENDER. Its ink is the only bright thing in the Hollow.
W|Does existing come with a receipt?
W|Where do I sign for this bat?
Y|Hello! Uploading victory! Striking this address now!

scenes.name: Six Deliveries

lines: W|They are fast, I'll give them that. Pay up.
W|I know how to hit a thing, Slice.

scenes.name: The Notice
scenes.beat: The Courier arrives with a clipboard and reads the order out.
lines: S|The Courier. It reads the order out, then it lands.
W|Then it can read me the bill.
S|Red is where it lands. Move, or break it.

scenes.name: Notice Undelivered

lines: N|The notice drifts down. Nobody has signed it.

scriptedSetPiece.name: The Courier's Notice
scriptedSetPiece.text: The Courier lifts the notice; a red mark fills on the circle's ground over two seconds. Break the wind-up with a tenth of its health, or stand in the mark and take the stamp yourself. Wallit takes the stamp: Slice is spared.

choices.prompt: The notice lies on the grass. What does Wallit do?

options.label: Pocket it. 'Evidence.'
options.now: W|Evidence. Every bill has a paper trail.
options.later: Ch5 The Stamp, Reversed: Wallit presses the stamp to this notice first and Slice says 'You kept it.' W: 'I keep receipts.'

options.label: Tear it. 'Void.'
options.now: W|Void. I don't take bills I didn't order.
options.later: Ch5: Wallit has to pull a page off the wall instead; Slice: 'You tore the first one. We take another.'

choices.prompt: First bolts in hand. Slice says nothing. Wallit decides.

options.label: Hold one out to Slice. 'Your cut.'
options.later: Ch3 The Belt: Slice says 'It isn't' and adds 'You tipped. Cleared things don't tip.' Ch6: she files the bolt into the door.

options.label: Keep every bolt. 'Overhead.'
options.now: W|Overhead. Don't look at me like that.
options.later: Ch3 The Belt: Slice says only 'It isn't.' The line lands drier.

scenes.name: The Gate

lines: W|Hello? Sender? I'd like a word, and a receipt.
N|The wall answers. From the other side, pressed through the dark, the same stamp: RETURN TO SENDER.

N|At the foot of the gate, a postmark is torn into the stone. Half of it is his.

scenes.name: Past the Broken Gate
scenes.beat: A sunken yard of hooks and unfinished chassis.
lines: N|Past the broken gate the ground drops away into a yard lit by lamps. Rows of Yo Bot chassis hang on hooks.
H|Hello! I am... not finished! Uploading victory?

scenes.name: The Belt
scenes.beat: Cleared things ride past: a hat, a clock, a small bell.
lines: N|A slow belt carries flat, cleared things past the hooks: a hat, a clock, a small bell.
W|Cleared things. Somebody's hat. Somebody's clock. That could be me.
N|The belt runs on into a chute lit by a single red lamp. The lamp is a lens. It turns toward the Hollow, and the circle blinks once.
S|Pull the lever. The belt stops. The Crew stops.

scenes.name: The Lever
scenes.beat: He pulls it. The hooks swing empty.
lines: W|One lever. No sign. Somebody trusts the floor.
W|Those bolts are the same ones they've been paying me.
N|The hooks swing empty. The belt stops with a cleared clock still on it, ticking.

scenes.name: Order, Read Aloud

W|It reads it like a bill of lading.

scriptedSetPiece.name: The Belt Stops
scriptedSetPiece.text: At the lever the whole yard's sound cuts at once: conveyors, lamps, chirps. For three seconds only the cleared clock ticks. Then the Half-Built, hanging by one hook, asks: 'Finish me?' Slice: 'Don't.' Wallit: 'Wasn't going to. Not for free.'

options.later: Foreman phase two begins with a stalled line and a shorter march; Slice: 'It reads what it is handed.'

choices.prompt: The Half-Built hangs by one hook and wants finishing.

options.label: Leave it on the hook.

options.label: Cut its hook. Let it drop.
options.now: H|Hello! Thank you? Uploading... I do not know what.
options.later: Ending: a half-built Yo Bot is among the things given a door; its line is 'Hello! I am... received?'

scenes.name: The Long Walk

lines: W|They're not bigger Yo Bots. They're... deliveries.

scenes.name: Served

lines: N|The Spider Bot folds one leg and holds out a paper. It waits.

scenes.name: Refusals
scenes.beat: The Server offers three times. Each is refused with a blow.
lines: V|This is your third offer. After this, service is by force.
S|It's polite. That's the worst of it.

scenes.name: Undelivered

scriptedSetPiece.name: The Paper Is Out
scriptedSetPiece.text: The Server stops a step short of the circle, folds a leg and holds the paper out. It will not strike while the paper is out. Wallit refuses it by landing a blow. It backs off and offers again, three times. Its health cannot fall below 70% until the third refusal.

choices.prompt: The paper is out. Taking it ends the offer.

options.label: Refuse it. Strike the Server's claw.
options.later: Canon fight: three refusals, then force.

options.label: Take the paper and read it.
options.now: N|The paper reads: STRIKE THIS ADDRESS. No signature. The Server's leg unfolds.
options.later: The Server skips the second offer and winds up at once but with a shorter march; Ch5 the reading opens with Wallit already knowing the order is unsigned: W: 'I've seen it. I don't need to be told.'

choices.prompt: The Server's paper is for Slice. Who answers?

options.label: Wallit steps between: 'Talk to me.'
options.now: V|Delivery is to the named address.
options.later: Canon: Slice stays at the circle.

options.label: Slice answers herself: 'Refused.'
options.later: Ch6 Filed: Slice writes the door number without being asked; Wallit: 'You answered it first.'

setPiece.name: The Doors Open
setPiece.text: Every lost thing set in the ring rises one at a time and a door appears behind each. The Courier's clipboard (if notice_kept) is among them; so is a half-built Yo Bot (if Ch3 unhook). The last door is Slice's. It has a number in her handwriting. If door_for_both it has two numbers.

openQuestions.q: Who is the Department? A person, a machine, a building, a rule?
openQuestions.assumed: A process with no face; its parts are the bots, the walls and the stamps.

openQuestions.q: Did Slice once work for the Department's order, and why did she stop?
openQuestions.assumed: Yes, once. Why is never said; her care is shown, not told.

openQuestions.q: What is Wallit: a lost thing, a made thing, or a filed thing that went wrong? Whose money was in him?
openQuestions.assumed: Unsaid. The torn postmark is half his; the other half is never found.
No one. The stamp is automatic.

openQuestions.q: Are the cleared things on the Floor alive?
openQuestions.assumed: No, but Wallit fears they might be; Ending lets J decide whether they wake.

openQuestions.q: Does a Half-Built Yo Bot count as unfiled?
openQuestions.assumed: Yes; it appears in the ending only if Ch3 unhook was chosen.

openQuestions.q: Should the choices change real outcomes, or only later lines?
openQuestions.assumed: Only lines and one scene variant, so no save-format change is needed beyond a flag word in the case file.

openQuestions.q: Should choices be made in dialogue boxes (Cutscene.cs supports none yet) or in the world?
openQuestions.assumed: In the dialogue box with two buttons; requires a Cutscene.cs choice page.
Unknown. It reads from a clipboard that is blank when examined.

openQuestions.q: Why 30 waves in Arcade and 3 in Chapter 6?
openQuestions.assumed: Arcade is the Department trying again; the campaign is the Department being answered.

openQuestions.q: Does the player ever get an address of their own?
openQuestions.assumed: Wallit is on the books through the circle only. A sequel hook could give him a door of his own.

openQuestions.q: Should every line have a Hawkes Gen voice?
openQuestions.assumed: Subtitles first; Wallit and Slice voiced where files exist.
